key_insight: TrajectoryFlowNet learns both how particles travel and how the surrounding fluid flows from very limited trajectory measurements. Its physics-informed approach was validated in simulations and blood-flow experiments.
problem_solved: Reconstructing flow fields and predicting long-range particle paths when only sparse trajectory measurements are available.
method: Combines a Lagrangian view of moving particles with an Eulerian view of flow at fixed locations.
Uses physics-informed learning to jointly predict particle trajectories and flow fields from limited measurements.
Validates predictions using simulations and blood-flow experiments.
impact: The work illustrates how physical constraints can help AI extract more information from sparse observations. It offers a promising approach for practitioners building data-efficient models of fluid motion.
visual_elements: Sparse measured trajectory points transforming into continuous predicted particle paths.
Side-by-side diagram contrasting particle-following and fixed-location views of fluid motion.

Validation panels showing simulation and blood-flow experiment settings.
paper_title: Lagrangian–Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet
paper_authors: Jingdi Wan, Hongping Wang, Bo Liu, Xiaolei Yang, Xiaodong Hu
